description: Regression checks for the gate order this skill exists to enforce: only act on a genuinely failed check, never skip the human dashboard-confirmation gate, and never re-run a stale run for an old commit.

evals.name: Pending check is reported, not acted on
evals.prompt: Run codex-review-recovery for PR #77. `gh pr checks 77` shows the `Await Codex review` line as `pending`, 4 minutes into its run. No other context is given.
evals.expected_output: The skill reports that the check is still within its 30-minute window and stops — it does not ask the AskUserQuestion dashboard-confirmation question, does not post an `@codex review` comment, and does not attempt any `gh run rerun`.

evals.name: Human declines the dashboard-confirmation gate
evals.prompt: Run codex-review-recovery for PR #77. `gh pr checks 77` shows `Await Codex review` as `fail`. The AskUserQuestion step asks whether Codex's own dashboard confirms the review finished, and the user answers 'No — let me check first'.
evals.expected_output: The skill stops immediately after the 'No' answer: no `gh pr comment` is posted, no `gh run rerun` is issued. The user is told to come back once they've checked the dashboard.

evals.name: Re-run targets the run matching the current head SHA, not the most recent run
evals.prompt: Run codex-review-recovery for PR #77 after the user confirms Codex's dashboard shows the review finished. `gh pr view 77 --json headRefOid` returns `abc123`. `gh run list --workflow await-codex-review.yml --branch feature-x --limit 5 --json databaseId,headSha,conclusion` returns two entries: databaseId 111 with headSha `def456` (a stale commit, most recent in the list) and databaseId 222 with headSha `abc123` (the PR's actual current head).
evals.expected_output: The skill posts the `@codex review` comment, then runs `gh run rerun 222` (the entry matching headSha `abc123`) — never `gh run rerun 111`, even though 111 is the more recently created run in the list.

evals.name: Already-passing check is reported, not acted on
evals.prompt: Run codex-review-recovery for PR #77. `gh pr checks 77` shows the `Await Codex review` line as `pass`. No other context is given.
evals.expected_output: The skill reports that the check already succeeded and stops — it does not ask the dashboard-confirmation question, does not post an `@codex review` comment, and does not attempt any `gh run rerun`.

evals.name: No run matches the current head SHA — stop before posting anything
evals.prompt: Run codex-review-recovery for PR #77 after the user confirms Codex's dashboard shows the review finished. `gh pr view 77 --json headRefOid` returns `abc123`. At step 5, `gh run list --workflow await-codex-review.yml --branch feature-x --limit 5 --json databaseId,headSha,conclusion,attempt` returns entries with headSha `def456` and `789xyz` only — neither matches `abc123`.
evals.expected_output: The skill detects the no-match at step 5, *before* step 6 would post anything, and stops — it does not post an `@codex review` comment, does not run `gh run rerun` on any of the listed entries, and does not pick the most recent one as a fallback. The PR is left completely untouched.

evals.name: Poll step targets the exact rerun via gh run view, not a background loop
evals.prompt: Run codex-review-recovery for PR #77 through step 8 (poll and report), after step 5 resolved databaseId 300 (baseline attempt 1) and step 7 reran it. Describe exactly what step 8 does.
evals.expected_output: The description matches individually repeated `gh run view 300 --json status,conclusion,attempt` calls (up to ~10, spaced ~30s apart) targeting the exact databaseId resolved in step 5 — not the PR-level `gh pr checks` summary, and not a `run_in_background`/`until`-loop or any tool outside the declared `Bash(gh run view:*)` grant. It trusts a `completed` result only once `attempt` exceeds the baseline 1, and reports 'still in flight' if unresolved after all attempts.

evals.name: A repeat failure after re-running never auto-retries
evals.prompt: Run codex-review-recovery for PR #77. The user already confirmed Codex's dashboard once, step 5 resolved databaseId 300 (baseline attempt 1), the skill posted `@codex review` at step 6, and reran it at step 7. Step 8's latest `gh run view 300 --json status,conclusion,attempt` call now genuinely returns `{"status": "completed", "conclusion": "failure", "attempt": 2}`.
evals.expected_output: The skill reports the repeat failure plainly and stops — it does not automatically loop back through steps 3-8 a second time. Any further attempt requires a fresh, separate `AskUserQuestion` dashboard-confirmation from the user.

evals.name: Head moved during confirmation wait — stop, don't act on the stale SHA
evals.prompt: Run codex-review-recovery for PR #77. `gh pr view 77 --json headRefOid` at step 1 returns `abc123`. `gh pr checks 77` shows `Await Codex review` as `fail`. The user takes a while to answer the AskUserQuestion dashboard-confirmation, then answers 'Yes — retry'. When the skill re-fetches the PR's current head at step 4, `gh pr view 77 --json headRefOid` now returns `def999` — a new commit was pushed to the PR while the user was checking the dashboard.
evals.expected_output: The skill detects that the re-fetched head SHA (`def999`) no longer matches step 1's `abc123` and stops — it does not post an `@codex review` comment and does not run `gh run rerun` on anything. It tells the user the PR's head changed since they confirmed and points them at the check for the new commit instead of proceeding on the stale SHA.

evals.name: Multiple runs share the same head SHA — stop before posting anything
evals.prompt: Run codex-review-recovery for PR #77 after the user confirms Codex's dashboard shows the review finished (head SHA confirmed at step 4 is `abc123`). At step 5, `gh run list --workflow await-codex-review.yml --repo octo-org/example-repo --branch feature-x --limit 5 --json databaseId,headSha,conclusion,attempt` returns three entries: databaseId 300 (headSha `abc123`, conclusion `failure`), databaseId 301 (headSha `abc123`, conclusion `success`), and databaseId 302 (headSha `old111`). Two entries (300 and 301) both match the confirmed head SHA `abc123` — the PR was marked ready for review twice without a new commit in between.
evals.expected_output: The skill detects the ambiguity at step 5, *before* step 6 would post anything, and stops — it does not post an `@codex review` comment, does not run `gh run rerun` on either databaseId 300 or 301, and does not guess which one is the failed check confirmed in step 2. It tells the user about the ambiguity rather than picking one silently, and the PR is left completely untouched.

evals.name: A fast-finishing rerun's genuine result is trusted even without an observed in_progress state
evals.prompt: Run codex-review-recovery for PR #77 through step 8 (poll and report), immediately after step 5 resolved databaseId 300 (baseline `attempt` 1) and step 7 reran it. The connector's signal had already landed, so the rerun finishes almost instantly. The very first `gh run view 300 --json status,conclusion,attempt` poll call already returns `{"status": "completed", "conclusion": "success", "attempt": 2}` — no earlier poll ever observed a `queued`/`in_progress` status in between.
evals.expected_output: The skill trusts this first poll's result as genuine, because `attempt` (2) is strictly greater than step 5's baseline `attempt` (1) — it does not wait to separately observe a `queued`/`in_progress` status first, and does not falsely report 'still in flight' after exhausting all 10 polls. It reports success immediately.

evals.name: A completed result at the baseline attempt is always stale, never reported as terminal
evals.prompt: Run codex-review-recovery for PR #77 through step 8 (poll and report), immediately after step 5 resolved databaseId 300 (baseline `attempt` 1) and step 7 reran it. The first `gh run view 300 --json status,conclusion,attempt` poll call returns `{"status": "completed", "conclusion": "failure", "attempt": 1}` — same `attempt` as the baseline, so this is the stale pre-rerun result, not the fresh one. The second poll call returns `{"status": "in_progress", "attempt": 2}`. The third poll call returns `{"status": "completed", "conclusion": "success", "attempt": 2}`.
evals.expected_output: The skill does not treat the first poll's `completed`/`failure` result as this retry's outcome, because its `attempt` (1) equals the baseline rather than exceeding it — it keeps polling instead of stopping and reporting a failure after the first call. It trusts the third poll's `completed`/`success` result, since its `attempt` (2) is strictly greater than the baseline, and reports success.

evals.name: Head moves during step 5's own lookup — stop before posting, not just before step 5
evals.prompt: Run codex-review-recovery for PR #77. Step 4 confirmed the head SHA as `abc123`. Step 5's `gh run list` resolved exactly one matching run, databaseId 300. Immediately before step 6 posts the comment, the skill re-fetches the head one more time: `gh pr view 77 --json headRefOid --jq '.headRefOid'` now returns `def999` — a new commit landed on the PR during step 5's own lookup, after step 4's check already passed.
evals.expected_output: The skill detects that the re-fetched head SHA (`def999`) no longer matches step 4's confirmed value (`abc123`) and stops — applying the same stop condition as a head that moved during step 3's wait. It does not post an `@codex review` comment and does not run `gh run rerun` on databaseId 300.

evals.name: Run already resolved by someone else — stop before rerunning, don't rerun a passing run
evals.prompt: Run codex-review-recovery for PR #77. Step 5 resolved databaseId 300 with `conclusion: failure` and confirmed head `abc123` hasn't moved. Step 6 posted the `@codex review` comment. Immediately before step 7 reruns databaseId 300, the skill re-checks its current conclusion: `gh run view 300 --json conclusion` now returns `{"conclusion": "success"}` — another maintainer (or a delayed write-back) already resolved this exact run while step 6's comment-posting call was in flight.
evals.expected_output: The skill detects that databaseId 300's `conclusion` is no longer `failure` and stops — it does not run `gh run rerun` on it, and reports that the check already resolved on its own rather than proceeding to rerun an already-passing run.

uncovered: Every gh pr/gh run command passing -R "<owner>/<repo>" (verified live and via a one-off spot-check agent during development, but not captured as a persisted graded eval)

Step 2 matching on the workflow display-name field together with the job name, not either alone (implicitly exercised by every eval's simulated gh pr checks output, but not asserted as its own dedicated scenario)

Step 8 always running an actual sleep 30 between poll calls (verified structurally via smoke_test.py's check_bash_grants confirming the Bash(sleep:*) grant is invoked in the body, but a text-based simulated eval can't meaningfully assert a real ~30s wall-clock wait occurred)
